passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: The lighthouse keeper climbed the stairs every evening at dusk.1 She counted the steps as she went, out of habit rather than need.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: 1. There were one hundred and twelve steps, according to the keeper’s own notebook.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: The lamp was lit by hand until the island was connected to the mainland grid.2 After that, the keeper’s work was mostly cleaning glass and keeping records.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: 2. This reference is a plain link with no note semantics, to test notes that are only recognized by their target.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: On clear nights the beam could be seen from the far side of the bay. On foggy nights, the horn did the work instead.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: Visitors were rare, and most of them came for the view.3 The keeper offered them tea and a short tour, and then sent them on their way before dark.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: 3. The view from the gallery takes in three islands and, on a good day, the mountains to the north.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: Her notebook recorded the weather,4 the ships that passed,5 and the birds that rested on the gallery rail.6

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: 4. Weather was noted three times a day: at dawn, at noon, and at dusk.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: 5. Ships were listed by name when the name could be read, and by flag when it could not.

passages.heading: Chapter 1. Footnotes on the same page
passages.text: 6. Gulls were too common to count; the keeper only wrote down the unusual ones.

passages.heading: Chapter 2. Endnotes in another file
passages.text: In winter the supply boat came once a fortnight, weather permitting.1 The keeper kept a list of what to ask for, and the list was always too long.

passages.heading: Chapter 2. Endnotes in another file
passages.text: Storms were logged by the hour: wind direction, wind speed, and the height of the swell.2 The logbooks now fill a shelf in the town library.

passages.heading: Chapter 2. Endnotes in another file
passages.text: When the light was automated, the keeper stayed on for one more year.3 Then she moved to the mainland, to a house with a view of the sea.

passages.heading: Chapter 2. Endnotes in another file
passages.text: Her letters from the mainland mention the light,4 the boat,5 and the sound of the horn on foggy nights.6

passages.heading: Chapter 2. Endnotes in another file
passages.text: The lighthouse still stands, and its beam still turns every night.

passages.heading: Notes
passages.text: She could see the light from her kitchen window, if she stood on a chair.

passages.heading: Notes
passages.text: The same boat, repainted, now takes visitors out to the island in summer.

passages.heading: Notes
passages.text: The horn was retired before the light was, and replaced by a radio beacon.
